policy: Frozen English bytes remain untouched. Deterministic defects confirmed by the shared audit are repaired in Marathi bodies, carry adjacent stable keyed notes, and are verified by projecting only the documented deltas back to the frozen formula structure. Additional MRSIZ findings remain separately identified.

audit.consultation_stage: Exact frozen source and each immediately controlling formula, table, definition or proof scope were read; OLSIZ-001 through OLSIZ-007 are applied, while OLSIZ-008 through OLSIZ-010 are reserved for OLP-0039 and OLP-0040.

issues.finding: The header and formula rows include f(7), whose value is -3, but the final value row stops at 3 and omits -3.
issues.action: Inserted the missing -3 beneath f(7) in the Marathi table and added the adjacent keyed note; frozen English bytes remain unchanged.
alternatives: Leave the omission and annotate only
issues.uncertainty: None about the value; the controlling formula gives -3.
issues.review_question: Is the inserted -3 cell and adjacent Marathi source note the clearest correction?
issues.required_translation_handling: Add -3 in the value row and an adjacent OLSIZ-001 source-correction note.

issues.finding: The statement uses the finite initial segment 0 through n while the proof obtains 0 through n-1; the parameter is implicitly renamed.
issues.action: Preserved both endpoints and added an adjacent clarification that they describe the same family after reindexing.
issues.uncertainty: No mathematical uncertainty; this is a Marathi-lane explanatory observation outside the shared deterministic-defect list.
issues.review_question: Would an explicit parameter renaming be clearer than the current adjacent note?

issues.finding: The phrase 'complement of a finite set Nat' is malformed and omits the relation between the finite set and Nat.
issues.action: Rendered the body as the complement in Nat of a finite subset of Nat and added the adjacent keyed note.
alternatives: Rely on the following equivalence without a note
issues.uncertainty: None about the intended relation; the following formula controls it.
issues.review_question: Does the Marathi wording state both the ambient Nat and the finite-subset relation without redundancy?
issues.required_translation_handling: State 'the complement in Nat of a finite subset of Nat' (or an exact language-equivalent) and add an adjacent OLSIZ-002 note.

issues.classification: confirmed mathematical defect caused by injective-versus-bijective mismatch
issues.finding: A pairing function is defined only as an injection A×B→Nat, so its inverse is generally partial and is not an enumeration unless the pairing function is surjective.
issues.action: Separated the surjective case from the general range-restricted inverse argument and added an adjacent note.
alternatives: Assume surjectivity only in the exercise
issues.uncertainty: No mathematical uncertainty; this is an additional Marathi-lane finding outside the shared audit.
issues.review_question: Should the exercise retain both cases or simply assume a bijective pairing function?

issues.finding: The prose repeats the family (2,m) where it is enumerating successive rows.
issues.action: Replaced the second (2,m) occurrence by (3,m) in the Marathi body and added the adjacent keyed note.
alternatives: Retain both (2,m) occurrences and explain in prose
issues.uncertainty: None; the following table fixes the intended row family.
issues.review_question: Is the direct (3,m) correction and note preferable to retaining the duplicated displayed family?
issues.required_translation_handling: Replace the second (2,m) by (3,m) and add an adjacent OLSIZ-003 note.

issues.action: Replaced the unbound s_k and s_k(n) forms by one bound output name s and s(n), and added the adjacent keyed note.

issues.required_translation_handling: Use one bound output name, such as s, consistently in the characteristic-sequence definition and add an adjacent OLSIZ-004 note.

issues.finding: The displayed h(n) is explicitly a finite string of n zeros, but h is declared to map into the set of infinite binary sequences.
issues.action: Appended an explicit infinite tail of ones after the n initial zeros, making every displayed value an element of Bin^omega, and added the adjacent keyed note.
alternatives: Use n zeros followed by an alternating infinite tail
issues.uncertainty: No codomain uncertainty; the chosen eventually-one family is one of several valid non-surjective examples.
issues.review_question: Is the n-zeros-then-ones family the clearest corrected non-surjective map for this warning?
issues.required_translation_handling: Use a valid infinite binary output and add an adjacent OLSIZ-005 note.
